none: The travel-prayer report does not explain or cite 84:13.
The report concerns the Khawārij and has no link to 84:13.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that true dreams began Muhammad's revelation, followed by solitary worship at Hira and Gabriel's three commands to read; Gabriel then gave the opening verses through 96:5.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ، زَوْجَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَخْبَرَتْهُ أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ كَانَ أَوَّلُ مَا بُدِئَ بِهِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report glosses taḥannuth in the cave as worship.
rows.anchor: فكان يخلو بغار حراء يتحنث فيه - وهو التعبد - الليالي أولات العدد

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Khadija reassures Muhammad that God will never disgrace him, citing his care for kin, truthfulness, generosity, and aid to people in need.
rows.anchor: قالت له خديجة كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا والله إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث وتحمل الكل وتكسب المعدوم وتقري الضيف

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
rows.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the messenger sent to Moses, predicts Muhammad's people will expel and oppose him, and says he would support him if alive.
rows.anchor: فقال له ورقة هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad during prayer, then retreated at an unseen barrier; the passage is applied to Abu Jahl, and the Prophet says angels would seize him limb by limb.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ هَلْ يُعَفِّرُ مُحَمَّدٌ وَجْهَهُ بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِكُمْ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The transmission leaves uncertain whether the revelation attribution was in Abu Hurayra's account or something that had reached him.
rows.anchor: لا ندري في حديث أبي هريرة أو شيء بلغه
